name: Josh W. Comeau
award: Listed among the 10 best custom & creative developer blogs (DEV Community roundup); widely cited for interactive hand-built MDX posts
why: Whimsical, physically-animated interactive explainers with a custom widget in nearly every article, built from scratch without UI libraries.

name: Jhey Tompkins
award: Community 'pick of the year' in State of CSS 2022; regularly featured in CodePen and Codrops demo roundups
why: Playful, detail-obsessed CSS/JS micro-interactions from a Google DevRel engineer who pushes what CSS can do.

name: Maxime Heckel (blog)
award: HN front page: 'Rendering the Sky, Sunsets, and Planets' 537 pts (2026), 'Crafting Painterly Shaders' 245 pts; Figma Config 2025 speaker
why: Dark, precise long-form shader/WebGL essays with embedded live playgrounds - a model of the quiet, technical design-engineer aesthetic.

name: Lynn Fisher (lynnandtonic)
award: Famous annual from-scratch portfolio refresh (Adobe XD interview); 2025 refresh case study posted to HN (Mar 2026)
why: Reinvents her portfolio every year as an experiment in surprising responsive design, starting from a blank CSS file.

name: Robin Noguier
award: Awwwards Site of the Day + Honorable Mention (dev Lorenzo Cadamuro); Noguier sits on the 2026 Awwwards jury
why: Interactive-designer portfolio with a WebGL project carousel and cinematic transitions; a much-cited reference portfolio.

name: Cyd Stumpel
award: Awwwards Site of the Day (Portfolio 2022, 7.36) with Developer Award; Smashing Magazine person of the week
why: Creative-developer portfolio known for accessible yet expressive page transitions (swup, GSAP, Three.js).

name: Jesse Zhou - Jesse's Ramen
award: Awwwards Honorable Mention (Mar 2022); featured in Codrops Collective #701; credited with landing him multiple job offers
why: Baked-lighting Three.js/Blender ramen shop as a portfolio - the archetypal viral 3D personal site.

name: Henry Heffernan
award: Show HN: 3D portfolio with late-90s aesthetic (2022), later widely shared as the 'computer inside a computer' portfolio (HN score modest: 29 pts)
why: A 3D desk scene that zooms into a working retro-OS monitor - the spectacular counterpoint to minimal portfolios.

name: Aristide Benoist
award: Awwwards Site of the Month (June 2021) for his portfolio; multiple SOTDs incl. In Cognita (Mar 2025)
why: Independent WebGL developer whose portfolios are benchmarks for typography-led motion and smooth image transitions.

name: Mathis Biabiany
award: Awwwards Site of the Day (Jun 2018, 7.56) for his portfolio; Honorable Mention Aug 2026
why: Dark black/blue/teal real-time 3D portfolio from an ex-Resn creative technologist; strong reference for light-in-darkness WebGL.

name: Eduard Bodak
award: Awwwards profile: 4 Sites of the Day, 6 Honorable Mentions
why: German designer-developer ('Crafting websites that feel good') known for clean, tactile motion and restrained layouts.

name: Louis Paquet
award: Awwwards Independent of the Year 2025; profile lists 1 SOTY, 2 SOTM, 40 SOTD
why: Montreal digital creative director (ex-Locomotive), currently the most decorated independent designer on Awwwards.

name: Bartosz Ciechanowski
award: Repeated #1 on Hacker News: Mechanical Watch 4298 pts, Moon 3128, Sound 3053, Bicycle 3014, GPS 2900
why: Hand-built interactive 3D explainer essays; the gold standard of precise, engineering-grade web storytelling.

name: Nanda Syahrasyad - Not a Number
award: HN front page: 'Build your own database' 547 pts (2025); 'An interactive guide to SVG paths' 343 pts
why: Interactive programming explainers with animated diagrams, in the Ciechanowski/Comeau tradition.

name: Craig Mod
award: Many HN front pages (e.g. 'Fast Software, the Best Software' 470 pts; 'Takkyu-bin' 342 pts)
why: Writer-photographer whose site and walk essays are admired for restrained, book-like typographic and photographic presentation.

name: Frank Chimero
award: Redesign called 'quite wonderful' by Jeremy Keith (Adactio); featured on the Responsive Web Design podcast
why: Designer-writer whose publicly documented redesign is a touchstone for thoughtful, typographic personal sites.

name: Jakub Krehel
award: Featured design-engineer interview in Lovers Magazine; known for 'Details That Make Interfaces Feel Better' and oklch.fyi
why: Slovak design engineer with a minimal, precise site whose interface-detail writing is widely shared on X.

name: Immersive Garden
award: Awwwards Agency of the Year 2025 (also Studio of the Year 2017/2018/2020)
why: Paris studio of luxury-grade WebGL experiences with cinematic lighting and materials.

name: Malvah
award: Awwwards Studio of the Year 2025
why: Brand-experience studio whose own site is an editorial, motion-rich showcase.

name: abeto (Messenger)
award: Awwwards Developer Site of the Year 2025 for 'Messenger'
why: Small studio crafting interactive 3D experiences; Messenger was the year's most technically celebrated WebGL piece.

name: Lando Norris (by OFF+BRAND)
award: Awwwards Site of the Year 2025 and Users' Choice 2025
why: The most celebrated spectacular site of 2025 - 3D helmet, bold type and kinetic scroll; included for contrast.

name: Locomotive
award: Awwwards Agency of the Year 2024 (and 2020; self-described 7x winner); own site SOTM Jun 2019 and Mar 2023
why: Montreal agency behind Locomotive Scroll; benchmark for smooth-scroll editorial agency sites.

name: Obys
award: Awwwards Studio of the Year 2023; CSSDA Studio of the Year 2020/2021/2023; repeated SOTDs
why: Ukrainian studio known for typographic, grid-driven sites and the Design Education Series.

name: Resn
award: Awwwards Agency of the Year 2017 and 2018
why: New Zealand pioneer of playful, experimental interactive web campaigns.

name: Active Theory
award: CSS Design Awards Agency of the Year 2021; Webby Production Company of the Year contender 2022
why: Creative-tech studio behind large real-time 3D/WebGL brand experiences; its own site is a WebGL showpiece.

name: basement.studio
award: Three Awwwards SOTDs in 2024 (KidSuper, Daylight, Next.js Conf) with Developer Awards; 2025 SOTDs for own site
why: Studio known for Vercel/Next.js Conf work - dark, technical, developer-culture aesthetic.

name: Hello Monday
award: Awwwards Site of the Day (Oct 2019, 7.85) for own site; Awwwards Agency of the Year 2013
why: Danish studio (now part of DEPT) famous for warm, crafted micro-interactions.

name: Collins
award: 8x Agency of the Year (Ad Age 2019-2026, D&AD 2021), as listed on its own site
why: Brand-design company with a confident, type-led site; reference for elite brand-studio presentation.

name: Pentagram
award: World's largest independent design consultancy; own site featured in DesignRush best-designs gallery
why: Restrained, image-led partner and project archive - the canonical 'let the work speak' studio site.

name: 14islands
award: Awwwards Agency of the Year nominee 2021
why: Stockholm studio known for refined, tasteful interactive and WebGL work.

name: Exo Ape
award: Awwwards: own site Site of the Month (May 2022); 16 SOTDs incl. 'Fluid Glass' (Mar 2026)
why: Dutch studio of polished, premium motion sites; its Fluid Glass work is directly relevant to glass-object visuals.

name: The Pudding
award: SND47 Best in Show (micro/small orgs) for story page design; SND46 World's Best Designed Digital; several 1000+ pt HN hits
why: Visual-essay publication that sets the bar for custom scrollytelling and data-driven storytelling.

name: Reuters Graphics
award: Ranked 4th among top award-winning publications at SND47; past Malofiej Best of Show (digital)
why: Wire-service graphics desk known for clean, precise data visualisation and 3D explanatory pieces.

name: Stephen Kent Johnson
award: Featured on Siteinspire (Minimal / Photography)
why: Leading interiors/architecture photographer whose site is a minimal, image-first grid with quiet typography.

name: Satoshi Watanabe
award: Featured on Siteinspire (Minimal, Photography, Grid Layout), Jul 2026
why: Photography and moving-image portfolio with an austere grid layout that lets the images carry the page.
